from itertools import product

# Literals are (predicate, subject, object, polarity).
def lit(predicate, subject="", obj="", positive=True):
    return (predicate, subject, obj, positive)

def opposite(x):
    return x[:3] + (not x[3],)

facts = {
    lit("negotiates", "ant", "stork"),
    lit("photograph", "dragon", "fish"),
    lit("hides_cards", "mannikin", "liger"),
    lit("located", "mouse", "Nigeria"),
    lit("money", "stork", 98),
    lit("neglects", "worm", "chihuahua"),
    lit("surrenders", "crow", "wolf", False),
    lit("trades_piece", "dalmatian", "stork", False),
}

plant = lit("builds_plant", "stork", "goat_fields")
shout = lit("shouts", "mouse", "beetle")
smile = lit("smiles", "mouse", "cobra")
call = lit("calls", "llama", "husky")

# Existential summaries are derived only from actual witnesses.
some_plant = lit("exists_plant_near_goat_fields")
some_photo = lit("exists_photo_of_fish")

def strict_closure(knowledge):
    result = set(knowledge)
    if lit("located", "mouse", "Nigeria") in result:
        result.add(lit("located", "mouse", "Africa"))
    if any(p == "builds_plant" and o == "goat_fields" and sign
           for p, s, o, sign in result):
        result.add(some_plant)
    if any(p == "photograph" and o == "fish" and sign
           for p, s, o, sign in result):
        result.add(some_photo)
    return result

# Every antecedent must hold. Rule 5 is grounded for the mouse:
# its other ground instances cannot affect the queried proposition.
rules = {
    1: ({lit("negotiates", "ant", "stork"),
         lit("trades_piece", "dalmatian", "stork", False)}, plant),
    2: ({some_plant}, opposite(shout)),
    3: ({lit("more_money", "stork", "walrus")}, opposite(plant)),
    4: ({lit("located", "mouse", "Africa")}, smile),
    5: ({lit("hugs", "mouse", "dinosaur"), smile}, shout),
    6: ({lit("has_musical_instrument", "llama")}, call),
    7: ({lit("works_in_agriculture", "mouse")}, opposite(smile)),
    8: ({some_photo}, opposite(call)),
}
preferred = {(3, 1), (5, 2), (6, 8), (7, 4)}

def closure(selected):
    knowledge = strict_closure(facts)
    while True:
        updated = set(knowledge)
        for number in selected:
            body, head = rules[number]
            if body <= knowledge:
                updated.add(head)
        updated = strict_closure(updated)
        if updated == knowledge:
            return knowledge
        knowledge = updated

# Exhaustively test all 256 rule-firing selections for a fixed point.
models = []
numbers = sorted(rules)
for bits in product((False, True), repeat=len(numbers)):
    selected = {n for n, bit in zip(numbers, bits) if bit}
    knowledge = closure(selected)
    applicable = {n for n, (body, _) in rules.items()
                  if body <= knowledge}
    defeated = {
        low for high, low in preferred
        if high in applicable
        and rules[high][1] == opposite(rules[low][1])
    }
    if selected == applicable - defeated:
        models.append((selected, knowledge))

print("Admissible rule fixed points:", len(models))
if not models:
    print("UNSUPPORTED")
    print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
else:
    statuses = set()
    for selected, knowledge in models:
        positive = shout in knowledge
        negative = opposite(shout) in knowledge
        status = (
            "proved" if positive and not negative else
            "disproved" if negative and not positive else
            "unknown" if not positive and not negative else
            "inconsistent"
        )
        statuses.add(status)
        print("Fired rules:", sorted(selected))
        print("Mouse shouts:", positive)
        print("Mouse does not shout:", negative)
        print("Rule 5 missing antecedents:",
              sorted(rules[5][0] - knowledge))

    if len(statuses) == 1 and "inconsistent" not in statuses:
        expected = next(iter(statuses))
        submitted = "proved"
        print("Expected result:", expected)
        print("Submitted result:", submitted)
        print("CHECK PASS" if expected == submitted else "CHECK FAIL")
    else:
        print("UNSUPPORTED: no unique consistent classification")
        print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
